title: Pass the U.S. Reciprocal Trade Act ("mirror" tariffs)
proposal: This section urges Congress to pass the U.S. Reciprocal Trade Act. It would let the President press countries with higher tariffs or trade barriers to lower them, and if they refuse, raise U.S. tariffs to match.
quote: In summary, passage of the USRTA would go a long way toward leveling the playing field for American farmers, ranchers, manufacturers, and workers
contested: Navarro (fair trade) view; Lassman's free-trade section disagrees

title: Consider a border adjustment tax on imports
proposal: This section suggests a conservative Administration consider a "border adjustment tax," which would stop companies from deducting the cost of imports and stop taxing income from exports.
quote: A conservative Administration might do well to look at such a tax as part of its trade agenda.
contested: Navarro (fair trade) view; Lassman's free-trade section disagrees

title: Decouple the U.S. economy from China
proposal: This section says further trade talks with China would be fruitless, and the better choice is to separate the U.S. economically and financially from China.
quote: the better policy option was to decouple both economically and financially from Communist China as further negotiations would indeed be both fruitless and dangerous.
contested: Navarro (fair trade) view; Lassman's free-trade section argues against decoupling

title: Expand tariffs to all Chinese products at blocking levels
proposal: This section recommends putting tariffs on all Chinese products and raising them high enough to block "Made in China" goods, at a pace that keeps access to essential items like key medicines.
quote: Strategically expand tariffs to all Chinese products and increase tariff rates to levels that will block out "Made in China" products
contested: Navarro (fair trade) view; Lassman's free-trade section disagrees

title: Give incentives to companies moving production from China to U.S.
proposal: This section recommends large financial and tax incentives for American companies that move production from China back to the United States.
quote: Provide significant financial and tax incentives to American companies that are seeking to onshore production from Communist China to U.S. soil.
contested: Navarro (fair trade) view; Lassman's free-trade section disagrees

title: Close the de minimis tariff loophole for Chinese goods
proposal: This section recommends stopping China's use of the "de minimis" exemption, which lets shipments worth less than $800 enter without tariffs.
quote: Stop Communist China's abuse of the so-called de minimis exemption, which allows it to evade the tariffs for products valued at less than $800.
contested: Navarro (fair trade) view; Lassman's free-trade section disagrees

title: Bar Chinese state-owned firms from U.S. government contracts
proposal: This section recommends banning Chinese state-owned companies from bidding on U.S. government contracts, such as for subway and transit systems.
quote: Prohibit Communist Chinese state-owned enterprises from bidding on U.S. government procurement contracts
contested: Navarro (fair trade) view; Lassman's free-trade section disagrees

title: Ban Chinese-made drones in U.S. airspace
proposal: This section recommends prohibiting the use of drones made in China in American airspace.
quote: Prohibit the use of Communist Chinese–made drones in American airspace.
contested: Navarro (fair trade) view; Lassman's free-trade section disagrees

title: Ban Chinese social media apps like TikTok and WeChat
proposal: This section recommends banning all Chinese social media apps, such as TikTok and WeChat, citing national security and data-theft risks.
quote: Ban all Chinese social media apps such as TikTok and WeChat, which pose significant national security risks
contested: Navarro (fair trade) view; Lassman's free-trade section disagrees

title: Ban Chinese investment in U.S. high-tech industries
proposal: This section recommends prohibiting all investment from China in high-technology industries.
quote: Prohibit all Communist Chinese investment in high-technology industries.
contested: Navarro (fair trade) view; Lassman's free-trade section disagrees

title: Bar U.S. pension funds from investing in Chinese stocks
proposal: This section recommends prohibiting U.S. pension funds from investing in Chinese stocks.
quote: Prohibit U.S. pension funds from investing in Communist Chinese stocks.
contested: Navarro (fair trade) view; Lassman's free-trade section disagrees

title: Delist Chinese stocks that fail U.S. audit standards
proposal: This section recommends removing Chinese stocks from U.S. exchanges if they do not meet U.S. accounting oversight standards, or else closing China's "A shares" market to U.S. investors and deregistering sanctioned Chinese companies.
quote: Delist any Communist Chinese stocks that do not meet Public Company Accounting Oversight Board standards
contested: Navarro (fair trade) view; Lassman's free-trade section disagrees

title: Block Hong Kong clearinghouses for U.S. investment in China
proposal: This section recommends prohibiting the use of Hong Kong clearinghouses as a pass-through for American money invested in mainland China.
quote: Prohibit the use of Hong Kong clearinghouses as transit points for American capital investing in the Chinese mainland.
contested: Navarro (fair trade) view; Lassman's free-trade section disagrees

title: Keep Chinese government bonds out of U.S. investor portfolios
proposal: This section recommends prohibiting Chinese government bonds from being included in U.S. investors' portfolios.
quote: Prohibit the inclusion of Chinese sovereign bonds in U.S. investors' portfolios.
contested: Navarro (fair trade) view; Lassman's free-trade section disagrees

title: End U.S. dependence on Chinese supply chains for key goods
proposal: This section recommends steadily reducing and eventually ending U.S. reliance on Chinese supply chains for items tied to national security, such as medicines, chips, rare earth minerals, and military parts.
quote: Systematically reduce and eventually eliminate any U.S. dependence on Communist Chinese supply chains that may be used to threaten national security
contested: Navarro (fair trade) view; Lassman's free-trade section disagrees

title: Sanction companies that help China's Great Firewall censorship
proposal: This section recommends sanctioning any companies, including American ones like Apple, that help China's internet surveillance and censorship system.
quote: Sanction any companies, including American companies like Apple, that facilitate Communist China's use of its Great Firewall surveillance and censorship capabilities.
contested: Navarro (fair trade) view; Lassman's free-trade section disagrees

title: Hire AI firms to disrupt CCP influence operations on social media
proposal: This section recommends ordering DHS and the Justice Department to contract with U.S. artificial intelligence companies to detect and disrupt social media operations and funding of Chinese Communist Party influencers and domestic groups, using public information.
quote: Order the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and Department of Justice to contract with U.S.-owned and U.S.-operated artificial intelligence companies
contested: Navarro (fair trade) view; Lassman's free-trade section disagrees

title: Expand DHS crackdown on Chinese counterfeit goods sold online
proposal: This section recommends that DHS renew and expand its crackdown on Chinese online sellers and the platforms and warehouses, such as Amazon, eBay, and Alibaba, used to flood U.S. markets with counterfeit goods.
quote: Reinvigorate and expand the DHS crackdown on the CCP's use of e-sellers (including third-party sellers) and the shippers and operators of major warehouses
contested: Navarro (fair trade) view; Lassman's free-trade section disagrees

title: Close all Confucius Institutes in the U.S.
proposal: This section recommends forcing the closure of all Confucius Institutes, Chinese government-linked centers at U.S. schools, which it calls propaganda arms of the Chinese Communist Party.
quote: Compel the closure of all Confucius Institutes in the U.S., which serve as propaganda arms of the CCP
contested: Navarro (fair trade) view; Lassman's free-trade section disagrees

title: Cut or end visas for Chinese students and researchers
proposal: This section recommends greatly reducing or ending visas for Chinese students and researchers to prevent spying and information gathering.
quote: Significantly reduce or eliminate the issuance of visas to Chinese students or researchers to prevent espionage and information harvesting.
contested: Navarro (fair trade) view; Lassman's free-trade section supports student exchanges with China

title: Create a commission on COVID-19 origins and damages from China
proposal: This section recommends a presidential commission or select congressional committee to investigate the origins and costs of COVID-19 and possible ways to collect damages from the Chinese Communist Party.
quote: through the establishment of a presidential commission or select congressional committee that would investigate the origins of the virus
contested: Navarro (fair trade) view; Lassman's free-trade section disagrees

title: Appoint a U.S. Trade Representative committed to fair trade
proposal: This section says the next President should choose a U.S. Trade Representative who understands trade law tools and is committed to a "fair, balanced, and reciprocal" trade agenda.
quote: the most obvious position to get exactly right is that of the United States Trade Representative.
contested: Navarro (fair trade) view; Lassman's free-trade section disagrees

title: Align key trade officials behind the fair-trade agenda
proposal: This section says the Under Secretary of Commerce for International Trade, the National Security Adviser, and top economic advisers should be chosen to support the President's trade agenda, including tariffs and anti-dumping cases.
quote: is the need to fill the position of Under Secretary of Commerce for International Trade wisely.
contested: Navarro (fair trade) view; Lassman's free-trade section disagrees

title: Keep non-trade issues out of trade agreements
proposal: This section says trade agreements should leave out unrelated provisions on labor, environment, and other rules, and handle those issues in separate negotiations. It also calls for ending "mission creep" in trade policy.
quote: trade policy should limit trade-unrelated provisions in trade agreements. This does not mean that conservatives should ignore international negotiations
contested: Lassman (free trade) view; Navarro's fair-trade section disagrees

title: End Section 232, 201, and 301 tariffs
proposal: This section recommends removing tariffs imposed under Sections 232, 201, and 301 (such as steel, aluminum, and China tariffs), saying the President can do this alone and Congress can also act.
quote: Implement tariff relief to help counteract inflation by reducing prices for affected goods as well as to strengthen supply chains and boost manufacturing.
contested: Lassman (free trade) view; Navarro's fair-trade section disagrees

title: Repeal the laws letting Presidents impose 232, 201, 301 tariffs
proposal: This section says Congress should repeal Sections 232, 201, and 301, the laws that let Presidents set these tariffs, so future Presidents cannot use them.
quote: Work with Congress to pass legislation repealing those provisions so future Presidents cannot abuse them.
contested: Lassman (free trade) view; Navarro's fair-trade section disagrees

title: Don't expand trade adjustment assistance; use cash if expanded
proposal: This section says the government should resist more spending on trade adjustment assistance for workers who lose jobs to trade. If it must grow, it should be direct cash, and trade-displaced workers should get the same benefits as other displaced workers.
quote: Resist calls for more spending on trade adjustment assistance, which is often hijacked for progressive ends.
contested: Lassman (free trade) view; Navarro's fair-trade section disagrees

title: Remove protectionist supply-chain rules (e.g., baby formula)
proposal: This section recommends removing trade restrictions it calls unnecessary, using the baby formula shortage as an example, and permanently loosening tariffs and labeling rules that keep imports out.
quote: Remove never-needed supply chain restrictions, which give families fewer places to which they can turn.
contested: Lassman (free trade) view; Navarro's fair-trade section disagrees

title: Accept allies' product safety standards (mutual recognition)
proposal: This section recommends agreements with allies such as the U.K., EU, and Japan so that products approved as safe there can be sold here, and vice versa. It says this would especially help with medicines and baby formula.
quote: Enact mutual recognition policies with allies. If a product is safe enough for European or Japanese consumers, then it is safe enough for Americans
contested: Lassman (free trade) view; Navarro's fair-trade section disagrees

title: Close the Export-Import Bank
proposal: This section recommends closing the Export-Import Bank, noting its charter expires at the end of 2026 and it will close unless Congress and the President renew it.
quote: Close the Export–Import Bank, which serves mainly to subsidize foreign buyers' purchases of goods from a handful of well-connected American manufacturers.
contested: Lassman (free trade) view; Navarro's fair-trade section does not address this

title: Repeal the Jones Act shipping law
proposal: This section recommends repealing the Jones Act, which requires ships moving goods between U.S. ports to be U.S.-built, owned, and crewed.
quote: a century-old "Buy American" maritime law that has decimated the U.S. shipbuilding industry.
contested: Lassman (free trade) view; Navarro's fair-trade section disagrees

title: Restore presidential Trade Promotion Authority
proposal: This section says the President should work with Congress to renew Trade Promotion Authority ("fast track") to speed up trade deals with the U.K., Switzerland, Taiwan, the EU, and other allies.
quote: Work with Congress to restore the President's Trade Promotion Authority, which would expedite the negotiation of trade agreements
contested: Lassman (free trade) view; Navarro's fair-trade section disagrees

title: Restore the WTO dispute resolution process
proposal: This section recommends bringing the World Trade Organization's dispute resolution system back to full strength. It notes the WTO's appeals body stopped working after the U.S. blocked new appointees.
quote: Restore the World Trade Organization's dispute resolution process to full strength.
contested: Lassman (free trade) view; Navarro's fair-trade section disagrees

title: Create a WTO successor open only to democracies
proposal: This section recommends that, if the WTO cannot be fixed, the U.S. build a successor, such as a "Global Free Trade Alliance," open only to free-market democracies and without special exemptions for developing countries.
quote: Create a successor to the WTO (assuming that it has been fatally wounded) that is open only to liberal democracies.
contested: Lassman (free trade) view; Navarro's fair-trade section disagrees

title: Rejoin the Trans-Pacific Partnership (TPP)
proposal: This section recommends rejoining the Trans-Pacific Partnership trade agreement, calling it a top priority for countering China.
quote: Rejoin the Trans-Pacific Partnership (TPP), whose 11 members are developing institutional trade norms in an important geopolitical region
contested: Lassman (free trade) view; Navarro's fair-trade section disagrees

title: Refocus the Indo-Pacific Economic Framework on trade
proposal: This section recommends changing the Indo-Pacific Economic Framework so it focuses only on trade and drops most non-trade issues like climate and labor policy.
quote: Reorient the proposed Indo-Pacific Economic Framework for Prosperity to focus only on trade issues
contested: Lassman (free trade) view; Navarro's fair-trade section disagrees

title: Pressure Beijing with allies; encourage people-to-people ties
proposal: This section recommends joining with allies to increase diplomatic pressure on China while encouraging cultural, student, and tourism exchanges between Americans and Chinese people.
quote: Strengthen diplomatic pressure (in concert with allies) against Beijing's abuses. Encourage cultural and intellectual engagement with the Chinese people
contested: Lassman (free trade) view; Navarro's fair-trade section favors decoupling and fewer Chinese student visas

title: Ease trade adjustment via zoning, licensing, and rule sunsets
proposal: This section says adjusting to trade could be made easier by loosening zoning and permit rules, reforming occupational licensing, and adding automatic expiration dates to new regulations.
quote: Trade adjustment could be made easier by regulatory reforms to remove its attendant friction.
contested: Lassman (free trade) view; Navarro's fair-trade section disagrees

title: Create a Regulatory Reduction Commission
proposal: This section suggests a presidentially appointed commission that would review federal regulations every year and send Congress packages of old or harmful rules to repeal.
quote: A presidentially appointed Regulatory Reduction Commission that would examine the Code of Federal Regulations each year and send repeal packages to Congress
contested: Lassman (free trade) view; Navarro's fair-trade section disagrees

title: Grant Jones Act exemptions wherever the law allows
proposal: This section says the Administration should use its own power to grant Jones Act exemptions wherever allowed, as often happens in hurricane season, while working with Congress to repeal the law.
quote: Jones Act exemptions wherever allowed, as currently happens most years during hurricane season, and working with Congress to repeal the Jones Act.
contested: Lassman (free trade) view; Navarro's fair-trade section disagrees

title: End China's developing-nation status in the WTO
proposal: This section recommends ending China's status as a developing nation in the WTO and other international groups, so it cannot use that status to get special treatment.
quote: End China's developing-nation status in the WTO and other international organizations.
contested: Lassman (free trade) view; Navarro's fair-trade section disagrees

title: Target individual Chinese firms instead of blanket tariffs
proposal: This section recommends acting against specific Chinese companies known for unfair practices like intellectual property theft, rather than placing broad tariffs on whole Chinese industries.
quote: Rather than blanket tariffs or non-tariff barriers aimed at entire Chinese industry sectors, firms that act in bad faith should be targeted individually.
contested: Lassman (free trade) view; Navarro's fair-trade section calls for tariffs on all Chinese products
